what: Adobe makes creative and document software: Photoshop, Illustrator, Premiere and Acrobat, sold as subscriptions, plus marketing and analytics software for large companies.
customers: Designers, photographers, video editors, students and businesses of all sizes; large enterprises for its marketing software.
money: Creative Cloud and Document Cloud subscriptions
marketing, analytics and commerce software for enterprises
moat: Its file formats and tools are the professional standard, taught in schools and embedded in agency workflows, so switching costs are high across whole teams.
risks: Generative AI tools let non-designers produce work that once needed Photoshop
Canva and Figma have taken share at the lower and collaborative ends
Growth has slowed to about 11% a year
The market has repriced the shares to a much lower multiple on AI concerns
opportunities: Gross margins near 89% and return on capital near 39% leave room to invest and still return cash
Its Firefly AI models are trained on licensed content, which matters to corporate customers
Document Cloud and Acrobat keep growing as a separate, large business
watch: Net new digital media annualised recurring revenue, the measure management guides to.
